payload.viable_set: The NO-REAL-ALTERNATIVES case, argued rather than manufactured. One candidate survives, and the reason is unusually strong here: the architecture is ruled in TWO independent places - se-v2-design §11 names the ladder and §18 records this transport as built and verified end to end - and v1 runs the same shape in production with its own ADRs. This iteration exists precisely BECAUSE that ruling was not followed, so re-deciding it would repeat the error. Twelve implementation alternatives were nevertheless enumerated and each eliminated on a stated failure: four breach a veto criterion or reproduce the current defect, three lose to a measurement already taken, the rest to duplication or surface. Recorded as degenerate, per the design's explicit allowance.
payload.complete_allocation: The single candidate allocates all fifteen functions, none orphaned: F1, F2 -> cluster A, the decision to speak; F3, F4, F5, F6, F7 and the F12 exit -> cluster B, the brief pipeline; F8, F9, F10, F11 -> cluster C, the summons; F15 -> cluster D, the answer; F13 report and F14 withhold-the-credential -> standing constraints over all four. INTERFACES: exactly two cross clusters. A -> C carries the decision to announce and the pairing, and it is mandatory. B -> C carries the brief's URL, and it is OPTIONAL BY CONSTRUCTION - the only interface in the design permitted to be absent. RATIONALE: that single optional edge is the ladder; everything else in the partitioning exists to keep cluster B's failure from reaching cluster C.
payload.criteria_traced: Every criterion carries its requirement lineage: C1 the owner is reached (R1, R8, R9, Q1) weighted VETO because reaching nobody is the failure this iteration removes; C2 the decision is readable (R4, R6) high, since a link that opens nothing is worse than none; C3 the host learns nothing (R5, R11) high, from the custodian tension; C4 failure is visible (R8, R12) high, because silent degradation hid the current defect for a day; C5 no new dependency surface (medium) from the account-maintainer tension. The weights come from the register and the five recorded stakeholder tensions, not from the candidate.
payload.front_recorded: A front of one, recorded as such rather than dressed as a comparison, with twelve eliminations each naming its failure: key in a query parameter or a second message; plaintext at rest; a separate decryptor; notifying optimistically; sleeping on folklore rather than checking; aborting when the brief fails; sending but staying silent; absolute URLs duplicated in config; the scheme-like answer:<topic> token that was actually shipped and that the owner found by tapping; inferring the mode from configuration; and always publishing.
payload.feasibility_checked: Not rough - PROBED live before this gate (run-bfd564ff9add), which is stronger than the state requires and is the direct answer to how this iteration's predecessor failed. Confirmed against the real services: encryption leaves no plaintext in the stored object; the store accepts an authenticated write with a bounded TTL; the page serves as text/html so it renders rather than downloads; the read-after-write window is ~1s, measured, refining the design's ~60s figure; and the relay accepts the full three-action card with a view link, preserving a gate's title, priority and tag. The one part that cannot be probed - the card's rendering and the tap itself - is D1, and it is this iteration's own release gate rather than a claim.
